articles.title: Oilers linked to blockbuster Dylan Larkin trade as Matthew Savoie-led package puts Detroit in a difficult position
articles.summary: NHL News: The Edmonton Oilers have been linked to a hypothetical trade for Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin, with a proposed package built around Matthew S.
articles.body: The Edmonton Oilers have been linked to a hypothetical trade for Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin, with a proposed package built around Matthew Savoie. The idea, posted through PuckGM, would send Savoie, Josh Samanski, Beau Akey and Edmonton’s 2028 third-round pick to Detroit for Larkin. It comes at a complicated moment for the Red Wings, who are dealing with Larkin’s trade request but have also made it clear they are not planning a rebuild. Larkin’s contract and full no-trade clause add another layer to a deal that looks far easier to construct on paper than it would be to complete.Could Matthew Savoie-led package be enough for Dylan Larkin?Savoie is the obvious centerpiece of the proposal. The 22-year-old winger was selected ninth overall by Buffalo in 2022 before joining Edmonton in the 2024 Ryan McLeod trade. He just completed his first full NHL season, producing 18 goals and 37 points in 82 games while playing alongside Connor McDavid. That gives Detroit a young player with real NHL experience rather than a prospect who still needs years to develop.The rest of the package is less certain. Samanski appeared in 24 NHL games last season, while Akey remains an intriguing young defenseman who has yet to make his NHL debut and is recovering from shoulder surgery. Add the 2028 third-round pick, and Detroit would receive several pieces, but none offers the immediate production Larkin provides.That matters because Larkin remains a productive center. He has spent his entire 808-game NHL career with Detroit, recording 276 goals and 643 points. He also scored 34 goals and had 67 points in 74 games during the 2025-26 season.Why would the Oilers have trouble making Dylan Larkin work?The biggest obstacle for Edmonton may not be the trade package. It could be the contract.Larkin is signed through 2030-31 at an $8.7 million annual cap hit and has a full no-trade clause. His camp has reportedly circulated a preferred destination list that does not include Edmonton.There is also the roster question. Edmonton already has McDavid and Leon Draisaitl carrying a combined $26.5 million cap hit. Adding Larkin would give the Oilers another expensive center and leave less room for the depth needed around their stars.Detroit faces its own problem. Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff has said a rebuild is “out of the question,” while owner Chris Ilitch said, “He could be here all year,” referring to Larkin.That makes the proposed deal especially difficult to square with Detroit’s stated direction. Savoie could become an important player, but moving Larkin for potential rather than established production would change the Red Wings’ timeline. articles.title: Rhea Ripley’s journey from Australia to becoming one of WWE’s biggest women’s stars, from the independent circuit to global championship glory and The Judgment Day
articles.summary: WWE News: The story of Rhea Ripley started, long before the title celebrations and WrestleMania appearances. Ripley was born Demi Bennett in Adelaide, South Aus.
articles.body: The story of Rhea Ripley started, long before the title celebrations and WrestleMania appearances. Ripley was born Demi Bennett in Adelaide, South Australia and started her professional wrestling career as a teenager on the Australian independent circuit. Her early training with Riot City Wrestling laid the foundations for a career that would eventually see her go from local competition to the biggest stages of WWE.The Australian grappler slowly honed a unique physical style and dominating presence that distinguished her from many of her peers. Her time in international wrestling and WWE’s developmental system finally got her in front of a much bigger audience, while character changes helped set the tone for the persona that became so synonymous with her rise.Rhea Ripley built her WWE identity in AustraliaRhea Ripley started training with Riot City Wrestling in Australia at the age of 16. Wrestling under the name Demi Bennett, she quickly got experience on the independent circuit against established performers. Her progress included two reigns as the RCW Women’s Champion, giving her an early championship resume before WWE became part of her career path.Her Australian performances eventually led to opportunities outside Australia. Ripley also competed internationally, including appearances in Japan, and gained experience that broadened her wrestling style and exposure. Those gigs helped establish her as a promising young performer before WWE signed her.Ripley had a tryout with WWE in the past but wasn’t accepted then due to age requirements. She would later join WWE and make an important step in her transition from Australian prospect to international performer by competing in the 2017 Mae Young Classic.YearCareer milestoneSignificance2013Rhea Ripley begins training in AustraliaStarts professional wrestling journey2014–2017Riot City WrestlingWins the RCW Women’s Championship twice2017WWE Mae Young ClassicIntroduced to a global WWE audience2018NXT UKBecomes inaugural NXT UK Women’s Champion2019NXTDefeats Shayna Baszler for the NXT Women’s Championship2021WrestleMania 37Defeats Asuka for the Raw Women’s Championship2022The Judgment DayBecomes a prominent member of the faction2023–2025WWE main rosterEstablishes herself as a major women’s division headlinerIn her early days in WWE, she was much different from the darker image that became synonymous with her career. The character changed over time, becoming more aggressive in appearance with the use of leather, spikes and a gothic-inspired aesthetic, a better reflection of her wrestling style that had become more physical.Rhea Ripley found championship success across WWE brandsRipley played a key part in the WWE’s expansion to NXT UK. In 2018, she became the first-ever NXT UK Women’s Champion by beating Toni Storm. The achievement placed her amongst the first major female Australian champions in WWE history and established her as a prominent figure on the emerging brand.Her success at the championship continued after she moved to NXT in the United States. Ripley beat Shayna Baszler for the NXT Women’s Championship in 2019, ending Baszler’s long reign and helping cement Ripley’s standing as one of WWE’s top young women’s wrestlers.Ripley’s other defining moment came at WrestleMania 37 in 2021, when she defeated Asuka to win the Raw Women’s Championship. It was one of WWE’s biggest annual stages, and another major step forward for her in her progression from developmental wrestler to main-roster headliner.She continued to add to her championship resume when WWE unveiled the Women’s World Championship. Ripley soon became entrenched in major premium live events, title programs and high-profile rivalries, cementing her status as a central figure in the women’s division.Rhea Ripley became central to The Judgment DayThe Judgement Day was all about why Ripley is so over is because of her character development. Her intimidating “Mami” persona gave her presentation a unique identity, and her physical style and confident promos cemented her as one of WWE’s most recognisable performers.Her being paired with The Judgement Day added a whole other layer to that character. Ripley was heavily involved in the faction with several other top WWE talents, helping to make the group one of the most visible acts on the main roster.Ripley’s profile rose, and she became a staple of the big storylines and premium live events for the WWE. Her mix of championship success, character work and high-profile rivalries helped elevate her from an Australian prospect to a global WWE star.Her journey also represents the growth of WWE’s international talent pipeline. articles.title: Could Connor Hellebuyck’s trade demand force the Winnipeg Jets into a major decision before NHL season starts
articles.summary: NHL News: It’s unclear what the future holds for Connor Hellebuyck with the Winnipeg Jets after the three-time Vezina Trophy winner publicly asked for a trade i.
articles.body: It’s unclear what the future holds for Connor Hellebuyck with the Winnipeg Jets after the three-time Vezina Trophy winner publicly asked for a trade in August. Things got worse when he didn't show up for training camp and the Jets suspended him.The 33-year-old goaltender made his stance known after making a private request for a move months ago. But Hellebuyck said he felt moving on was the best course of action for himself and his family, and Winnipeg has continued to explore its options.What does Connor Hellebuyck want from Winnipeg Jets?Connor Hellebuyck has asked the Winnipeg Jets to assist in facilitating a trade, but the team has not said where his preferred destination is. Team GM Kevin Cheveldayoff said the team is still looking for a solution that works for both sides.Hellebuyck has made public the decision about his future and family, but has not gone into detail on all of the factors behind the request. He said his position had not changed and moving on was the best path forward in a statement.The development comes after a tough 2025-26 season for Winnipeg. The Jets missed the Stanley Cup Playoffs after winning the Presidents’ Trophy last season, and Hellebuyck posted a 2.86 goals-against average and .895 save percentage in 57 games.What happened after Connor Hellebuyck missed camp?Hellebuyck was suspended by the organization after not reporting to Winnipeg Jets training camp on Sept. 16. The move comes in an already uneasy trade landscape as Winnipeg prepares for the 2026-27 NHL season.Cheveldayoff has said the Jets aren’t going to just move Hellebuyck without getting the right value in return. The goaltender still has five years left on his seven-year, $8.5 million average annual value deal.The Jets are in season preparation mode, and Cheveldayoff is working toward a potential resolution. Captain Adam Lowry had previously asked teammates to focus on preparing for the season, not have trade speculation take over the locker room.The organization also added Stuart Skinner, giving the Jets a veteran option in net while Hellebuyck remains away from the team. For now, the trade request is still pending, and the Jets are left with a major roster decision to make while trying to prepare for the NHL season ahead.The trade request of Connor Hellebuyck has become one of the biggest storylines in the NHL as the Winnipeg Jets seek a potential resolution; and the three-time Vezina Trophy winner did not report to training camp and was later suspended by the team.Hellebuyck has said that moving on is what is best for himself and his family, while Jets general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff continues to explore trade options. Winnipeg has also added goaltender Stuart Skinner, giving them another option while Hellebuyck is out. articles.title: Teenage badminton player Pitchamon Opatniputh becomes first athlete suspended after positive dope test at Asian Games 2026
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: Teenage Thai badminton player Pitchamon Opatniputh has become the first athlete to be provisionally suspended from the Asian Games 2026 after testing .
articles.body: Teenage Thai badminton player Pitchamon Opatniputh has become the first athlete to be provisionally suspended from the Asian Games 2026 after testing positive for a banned substance, the International Testing Agency (ITA) said on Monday.The 19-year-old, ranked 18th in the world in women's singles by the Badminton World Federation, returned a positive test for furosemide, a prohibited diuretic. The sample was collected during an out-of-competition test in Nagoya on September 17, two days before the formal opening ceremony of the Aichi-Nagoya Games.Opatniputh was scheduled to represent Thailand in the team event against China on Tuesday, but her provisional suspension means she cannot compete in the Asian Games.Provisional suspension takes immediate effectThe ITA said Opatniputh had been informed of the case and suspended with immediate effect pending its resolution under the World Anti-Doping Code and the Olympic Council of Asia's anti-doping rules.“This means that the athlete is prevented from competing, training, coaching, or participating in any activity, during the Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026,” the ITA said in a statement.Furosemide is a diuretic that increases the excretion of water from the body. It can be used to facilitate rapid weight loss and can also potentially mask the presence of other prohibited substances.Opatniputh, one of Thailand's leading women's badminton players, can challenge the provisional suspension. She has the right to request analysis of the B-sample and can also contest the suspension before the Court of Arbitration for Sport.The positive test comes early in the 16-day continental sporting event, which is being held across Aichi Prefecture and Nagoya until October 4.The case remains subject to the anti-doping process, and the provisional suspension does not by itself establish a final anti-doping rule violation. articles.title: Israel forfeits Chess Olympiad matches against Netherlands, Bulgaria; here's why
articles.summary: Chess News: Israel's men and women teams forfeited their sixth-round matches against the Netherlands and Bulgaria at the 46th FIDE Chess Olympiad in Samarkand on .
articles.body: Israel's men and women teams forfeited their sixth-round matches against the Netherlands and Bulgaria at the 46th FIDE Chess Olympiad in Samarkand on Monday after both opponents declined requests to change the schedule for Yom Kippur.The Israeli men's team was due to face the Netherlands in the Open section, while the women's team was scheduled to play Bulgaria. However, neither team showed up at the Silk Road International Exhibition Centre, leaving two empty tables and handing their opponents 4-0 wins by forfeit. The Netherlands had world No. 10 Anish Giri on Board 1.According to a FIDE statement, as quotd by Hindustan Times, Israel had formally requested that Monday's matches either start after 7:30pm local time or be moved to Tuesday, the tournament's rest day. The request was made because of Yom Kippur, considered the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.Teams are within their rights to reject requests that involve a change from the tournament's standard playing times. The Netherlands and Bulgaria did not agree to Israel's proposed changes, leading to the forfeits after the Israeli teams failed to appear for their matches.Israel had made a similar request ahead of the fifth round on Sunday, asking for an early start because of Yom Kippur. Singapore's men's team and Colombia's women's team agreed to the change, allowing those matches to be played as requested.Monday's matches followed a different course, with both the Netherlands and Bulgaria declining Israel's request.The forfeits came after another Israel-related incident in the opening round. articles.title: Muere Ida Amelie Robsahm, corredora de trail, por una caída en la montaña
articles.standfirst: La noruega, una de las grandes protagonistas del trail esta temporada y compañera de Sara Alonso, falleció tras sufrir un accidente en una ruta montañosa en su país
articles.summary: La noruega, una de las grandes protagonistas del trail esta temporada y compañera de Sara Alonso, falleció tras sufrir un accidente en una ruta montañosa en su país
articles.body: Ida Amelie Robsahm, corredora de trail running, murió a los 30 años tras sufrir una caída en Romsdalseggen, una de las rutas de montaña más conocidas de Noruega, su país natal. El accidente se produjo este sábado 19 de septiembre. Robsahm se encontraba acompañada por otra persona cuando cayó varios metros cerca de la cima. Un grupo de excursionistas avisaron a las fuerzas de seguridad. Los servicios de emergencia trasladaron a Robsahm en helicóptero al hospital donde posteriormente falleció. La muerte de Robsahm se produce sólo unos días después de que Kalie McCrystal, corredora de montaña canadiense, también falleciera mientras se encontraba en el Cervino. Robsahm despuntó en el Mundial de Montaña y Trail Running de Canfranc. Acabó cuarta en la distancia de 45 kilómetros. Esta temporada había sido también cuarta en la mítica Zegama-Azikorri. Entró en meta justo por detrás de la española Sara Alonso, su compañeroa en el equipo ASCIS. Alonso publicó un mensaje en su cuenta de Instagram con fotos de ella y Robsahm. "Ella ha sido mi gran descubrimiento este año y aunque apenas haya sido un año, la amistad creada ha sido infinita, igual que el dolor que todos sentimos. Una persona que no borró la sonrisa de su cara en ningún momento y con esa sonrisa la recordaré siempre", escribe Sara Alonso. "Nos quedaban muchas cosas por seguir viviendo, me quedo en paz sabiendo que se fue en un gran momento de su vida. Unos días antes por tu cumple, lo mejor que hice fue decirte lo especial que habías sido para mí y estoy feliz de que eso no se me quedara sin decir porque muchas veces olvidamos decirnos estas palabras. Cada zancada, kilómetro a partir de ahora serán por ella para siempre. Gracias por todo. Te quiero infinito", se despide la corredora española Tras Zegama, Robsahm fue segunda en el Maratón del Mont Blanc y luego acabó quinta en la modalidad OCC del UTMB. "Fue un shock. No se puede asimilar de inmediato. Ella estaba en un lugar, en un entorno donde se sentía tan cómoda. Nos la arrebataron. Deja una huella profunda. Es una tristeza inmensa en todos los sentidos", comentó Sindre Buraas, su entrenador, al medio noruego NRK. La trailrunner noruega brilló también el asfalto. En diciembre de 2025 debutó en el maratón en Valencia. Acabó con un tiempo de 2:29:57, el sexto mejor de una atleta de su país en la distancia.

articles.title: “Con Man”: ESPN’s Paul Finebaum Accuses Lane Kiffin of Faking His “Emotions” After Ole Miss Loss
articles.summary: ESPN’s Paul Finebaum is back in the anti-Lane Kiffin section after spending two weeks praising for LSU’s start to the 2026 campaign. After Ole Miss beat LSU...
articles.body:
ESPN's Paul Finebaum is back in the anti-Lane Kiffin section after spending two weeks praising for LSU 's start to the 2026 campaign. After Ole Miss beat LSU 32-24 in Kiffin's first return to Oxford, Finebaum questioned whether the LSU coach's words and demeanor told the full story.

"Lane Kiffin is still the same con man he was before he walked into that stadium, and you just saw it right there in living HD," Finebaum said on ESPN's First Take on Monday. "I mean, there's nothing believable about what he said."

Kiffin left Ole Miss for LSU last November after six seasons with the Rebels. He did not coach Ole Miss in the College Football Playoff after leading the program to an 11-1 regular season, but Saturday marked his first trip back to Oxford since taking the LSU job.

His return ended with a loss. No. 8 Ole Miss beat No. 7 LSU 32-24, surviving a second-half comeback before an interception in the end zone ended the Tigers' final possession. Finebaum said Kiffin looked uncomfortable throughout the night.

"He had built everything about going into that stadium and showing Ole Miss that he made the right decision," Finebaum said . "And ultimately he may have made the right decision, but he seemed out of sorts the entire game."

Finebaum also compared Kiffin's behavior to his old matchups with legendary coach Nick Saban, saying Kiffin had previously told him that he struggled to control himself when facing the former Alabama coach because he wanted to win so badly.

"He seemed uptight, really more so than any time I had seen him," Finebaum said.

The game itself gave Kiffin plenty to worry about because LSU fell behind 24-7 in the first half before mounting a comeback, and the Tigers eventually tied the game in the fourth quarter. But Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss responded with a drive that put the Rebels back in front.

Chambliss passed for 363 yards and two touchdowns while also running for the go-ahead score. He led a 75-yard touchdown drive after Ole Miss lost starting running back Kewan Lacy to a shoulder injury, then kept the ball on a 14-yard run for the score.

Ole Miss went for two afterward and converted, taking an eight-point lead with 6:14 left. That decision caught Finebaum's attention, too. He pointed to Pete Golding, the Ole Miss head coach who took over after Kiffin's departure, and noted that Golding might not have been viewed as an obvious head-coaching candidate when he was promoted.

Kiffin was left to explain a defeat that had been set up to be a major moment for his new program.

"I'm glad it's over. This was an emotional game for a lot of reasons," Kiffin said after the game. "A lot of life-changing experiences here. A lot of really good people that helped me through some really hard times."

He also acknowledged that the night had been different from a normal game. "Sometimes I don't act like it, but I'm a human, too," Kiffin added. "Congrats to those guys. They played really well. They deserved to win."

Finebaum saw it differently, as he said, "He [Kiffin] almost seemed like a zombie, and his team seemed to be representative of that."

Kiffin now has to move on from the loss with LSU sitting at 2-1. The Tigers host Texas A&M next Saturday, while Ole Miss takes its unbeaten 3-0 record to Florida .

articles.title: Kyle Long shares blunt defense of Caleb Williams showing vulnerability with injury
articles.summary: Kyle Long was tired of seeing Caleb Williams getting dragged through the mud for showing vulnerability in a tough moment.
articles.body:
Have you ever had the feeling that all of your hard work just went to waste? That, through no fault of your own, you just let down a football-obsessed city that embraced you like a family member? That, for a fleeting moment or two, your professional ambitions might never be the same?

That's likely what went through Caleb Williams 's mind on Sunday. After the Chicago Bears star quarterback went down in a heap late in a loss to the Minnesota Vikings with what turned out to be a non-major hamstring injury , anyone watching could tell how devastated he was about the injury. Even if Williams technically didn't suffer a "severe" injury, how he reacted wasn't necessarily all about pain tolerance. Which is A-OK! Sometimes, an injury reaction is not just about the injury itself!

However, this distinction unfortunately didn't sit well with folks who have an extremely antiquated and immature idea of masculinity and when a person is "allowed" to show any semblance of emotion and vulnerability.

The said current of toxicity did not sit well with former Bears offensive lineman and current CBS analyst Kyle Long . In response to some people predictably litigating just how animated Williams is allowed to be about getting hurt (which is pure, illogical nonsense when you think about it for more than five seconds), Long shared a perfect explanation about why Williams looked so crestfallen over what wound up being an injury that might cause him to miss a couple of games at most.

I couldn't have put it better myself. Williams understands the responsibility of being a star Bears quarterback in a city that has never had one before. He's a high-level athlete carrying the burden and pressure of being "The Guy" who could, hopefully, end a Chicago Super Bowl drought that's been going on for four decades. And for a little while there on Sunday, he thought he had lost everything he worked for on this front with such diligence and attention to detail.

There is nothing wrong with showing vulnerability in a tough injury situation. There is nothing wrong with him being emotional about getting hurt, no matter how severe it is. If anything, he should be applauded for wearing his heart on his sleeve and setting an example for all of us, rather than reacting like a stoic robot and holding it all in. Who are we to tell someone how they're allowed to react to any sort of injury or failure, intentional or unintentional? Do you know how shameful and embarrassing that sounds? Shouldn't we be better?

Any further thought process to the contrary needs to be dead and buried, both in sports and any other facet of life. Forever.

Kudos to Long for coming to Williams' defense. Kudos to Williams for unapologetically being himself and clearly not caring what other people think about how he operates as a football player and as a person.

articles.title: ESPN analyst reveals what it would take for Steelers to bench Aaron Rodgers
articles.summary: Week 2 was another rough one for Rodgers, but a benching isn't close just yet.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers dropped to 1-1 in the 2026 season after a Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots . Aaron Rodgers and the offense struggled again, this time not being bailed out by a terrible offense on the other side of the ball.

Rodgers struggled again in Week 2, and it wouldn't be a surprise if some Steelers fans began bringing up the question of benching him this season. But such an aggressive decision isn't likely to come.

But when could Rodgers get benched, if there is a scenario for the Steelers to bench him? ESPN's Dan Graziano revealed what it would take for Pittsburgh to bench Rodgers in his last NFL season.

ESPN analyst reveals when Steelers could bench Aaron Rodgers

"I simply do not believe that McCarthy would bench Rodgers in his final season for Mason Rudolph , Will Howard , or Drew Allar -- at least not until the Steelers are eliminated from postseason contention," Graziano writes.

So long as the Steelers have a chance to make the postseason, Rodgers will be the starter, according to Graziano. This should not be a surprise.

It's Rodgers' last season in the NFL before he retires. It would be shocking if Rodgers were benched in the middle of the season. His history should give him plenty of leash when it comes to being the Steelers' starting quarterback.

While there might be questions about how good he'll be on a weekly basis, the Steelers should be expected to stick by Rodgers until their playoff hopes are over.

As interesting as it would be to see Howard or Allar, two young quarterbacks, step into a starting role in regular-season games, that is reserved for the end of the season.

If the Steelers are eliminated from playoff contention, Rodgers could be benched to get a look at a younger quarterback. But such a scenario won't happen until much later this year.

Steelers fans should expect to see Rodgers remain as the starter going forward, even if he continues to struggle as he has through the first two weeks of the 2026 season.

Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow during Sunday's loss to the Commanders and is now trying to sort out how long he will be out of action as a result of the injury.

Daniels went for imaging on the elbow on Monday and head coach Dan Quinn said at a Monday press conference that he will now solicit opinions from specialists about the next courses of action.

Daniels suffered the same injury during the 2025 season and missed four games before returning to the lineup. He aggravated the injury in his return and then missed the final four games of the season. It's not clear if the past injuries will play a role in how Daniels and doctors choose to treat Sunday's dislocation.

Quinn said on Sunday that his team will "rally around" backup quarterback Marcus Mariota and confirmed on Monday that Mariota will start against the Seahawks in a Week 3 home game.

articles.title: Brewers prospect named the Southern League's most valuable player
articles.summary: Blake Burke, who finished the season with the Brewers' Class AAA team, also mashed in Class AA this year and was named Southern League MVP.
articles.body:
Blake Burke may no longer be a member of the Class AA Biloxi Shuckers, but the Milwaukee Brewers ' slugging first base prospect left a mark.

Burke was named the Southern League most valuable player Sept. 21, a nod to Burke's incredible season before an August promotion to Class AAA Nashville.

He was joined by teammates Jesús Made, Josh Adamczewski and Andrew Fischer on the 2026 Southern League All-Star Team . All are highly regarded prospects in the Brewers organization.

Burke hit 30 home runs at Biloxi – giving him a franchise-record 41 in his Double-A career – and led the league in batting average (.285) and OPS (.970). He became the first Southern League player with a 30-homer season since Wisconsin native Adam Brett Walker in 2015, and Burke needed just 88 games to reach that threshold.

All told, Burke played 96 games at Biloxi and stole 28 bases despite his 6-foot-3, 236-pound frame. Though he struggled in 31 games at Nashville (.635 OPS, four homers), his overall numbers for the year were still strong (.263 average, .889 OPS, 34 homers, 29 steals).

The 23-year-old left-handed bat, a 2024 Brewers first-round pick, is regarded as the No. 12 prospect in the organization by MLB Pipeline.

Burke and the rest of the Shuckers hit a franchise-record 178 home runs in 2026, shattering the old record of 154. Fischer, the Southern League all-star at third base, had a lot to do with it by parking 28 homers in 72 games with the Shuckers, with a 1.026 OPS for his portion of the season at Class AA.

Made, regarded as the top prospect in baseball, made the all-star team as a shortstop and spent all season with Biloxi. He finished with 14 homers, 91 RBIs, 37 steals and a .774 OPS. The 19-year-old's RBI count was the most in franchise history, breaking the mark of 90 by Jackson Chourio in 2023, and led the league.

Adamczewski, regarded as the No. 3 prospect in the organization, played in 66 games after promotion and made the Southern League all-star team as the left fielder. He had an .837 OPS in Biloxi with nine homers and eight steals. He started his career with a 12-game hitting streak, the longest stretch by any Shucker this season.

Burke is the first Brewers minor-leaguer to win a league MVP award since 2022, when both Jackson Chourio (Carolina League) and Jakson Reetz (Southern League) earned MVP honors.

Reetz, a catcher signed by the Brewers in the offseason before the 2022 season, left after they designated him for assignment in August of that season, and he elected free agency after clearing waivers. He had briefly gotten to the big leagues for two at-bats with Washington in 2021 and got back in 2024 with San Francisco for 14 at-bats.

On Sunday evening, the Indianapolis Colts dropped to 0-2 on the young 2026 NFL season with a tough overtime road loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in primetime. Many questioned head coach Shane Steichen's decision to go for a game-tying field goal late in overtime and give the ball back to Mahomes and company as opposed to just trying to win the game, but as the saying goes, hindsight is 20/20.

articles.title: Jalen Coker and Tyler Allgeier Lead This Fantasy Football Waiver Wire Debate After a Wild Week 2
articles.summary: The fantasy football waiver wire is heating up, with Jalen Coker and Tyler Allgeier emerging as intriguing options for managers looking to add depth.
articles.body:
When early-season injuries and unexpected depth chart shakeups hit, fantasy managers are forced to make high-stakes decisions on the waiver wire. Early in the season, two distinct types of targets emerge. The explosive wide receiver flashing immediate target-earning ability and the opportunistic running back inheriting a sudden, high-volume backfield role.

The debate centers on Jalen Coker (WR, Carolina Panthers) and Tyler Allgeier (RB, Arizona Cardinals). Both saw their valuation spike after unexpected usage trends. The debate hinges on what you value more in fantasy football. Is it high-upside receiving efficiency? Or is it floor-raising backfield volume?

Snap Percentage: 78% snap rate, establishing himself as a full-time route runner.

Routes Run/ Opportunities: 32 routes run on 38 dropbacks (84% route participation).

Red-Zone Usage: 2 red-zone targets, converting both into touchdowns.

Recent Role Change: shifted from a rotational slot option to a primary perimeter and power-slot hybrid, stepping up alongside Tetairoa McMillan

Snap Share: 57% snap share in favorable games, dropping to 34% in negative game scripts.

Efficiency: 3.59 yards per carry on early downs in Week 1, dropping to 2.0 YPC against Seattle's front in Week 2.

Red-Zone Opportunities: 3 red-zone carries, including 2 goal-line attempts inside the 5-yard line.

Team Situation: In line for a heavy workload while rookie Jeremiyah Love works through a lingering ankle injury and James Conner resides on injured reserve.

When comparing path to volume, Allgeier has a higher floor when game scripts favor the run , while Coker controls the higher-ceiling path to earned volume . Allgeier's volume is heavily game-script dependent. In Week 1 against the Chargers, Allgeier saw a backfield-leading 17 carries and logged a 60% rushing share in a close contest. In Week 2 against the Seahawks, as the Cardinals fell behind early, his workload evaporated to just 5 carries.

Coker earns his volume through route efficiency. His 28% target rate per route run (TPRR) and 4.31 yards per route run (YPPR) in Week 2 demonstrate elite target-earning ability. While WR targets fluctuate, Coker's 11.2 average depth of target and 26% target share suggest his volume comes with high-value air yards.

If you need a spot-start running back hoping for positive game script, Allgeier offers a solid solution. If you want high-value targets that can win a matchup on their own, Coker holds a significant edge.

Coker: Moderate floor (5-7 targets per game) with a high-end WR2 ceiling if he sustains a 20%+ target share.

Allgeier: Volatile floor (3-17 touches depending on game script) with a capped ceiling due to low passing-game involvement and 0 touchdowns scored through two weeks.

Coker: Positioned to consolidate his role as a primary receiving option alongside McMillan, maintaining an 80%+ route participation rate.

Allgeier: Rotational early-down back. While Conner is sidelined, he will share work with Love, likely capping out around a 45-50% overall backfield share.

The core distinction between these two waiver wire targets comes down to situational running back depth versus true season-long breakout potential. Allgeier is a short-term option for roster-strapped managers who is in desperate need of a running back and hoping for positive game scripts. Coker is a priority add for managers who's seeking an ascending, target-earning pass-catcher who possesses multi-week fantasy starter upside.

articles.title: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans has Nico Collins update after missing Bengals game
articles.summary: Houston Texans wide receiver Nico Collins did not play during Sunday’s loss against the Cincinnati Bengals.
articles.body:
After entering the 2026 NFL season with high expectations, the Houston Texans have stumbled into a 0-2 start.

Although the Texans lost their Week 1 matchup against the Buffalo Bills , the offense put together an encouraging performance after struggling last season. However, during the following week of practice, star receiver Nico Collins suffered a Grade 1 hamstring strain. This ruled him out of the Texans' Week 2 matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals .

Aug 13, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Houston Texans wide receiver Nico Collins (12) catches a pass before playing against the Las Vegas Raiders at Reliant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The Texans clearly felt Collins' absence, as the offensive woes that plagued them last season returned against Cincinnati. Houston suffered a frustrating 20-6 loss to the Bengals. The team moved the ball at times, but failed to find the end zone and struggled to consistently finish drives.

With Collins out, quarterback C.J. Stroud was without his most reliable weapon. In his absence, the team failed to convert any of their four zone opportunities and finished 5-for-17 on third downs. Oddly enough, the Texans actually outgained the Bengals by 107 yards. However, much of this yardage proved empty.

The Texans' rushing attack was nonexistent, accumulating only 18 rushing yards by running backs, meaning Stroud was forced to attempt 55 passes. With no threat of a ground game, the Bengals defense was able to lock the Texans' passing attack down as the field condensed in the red zone.

The Texans desperately need Collins back, but head coach Demeco Ryans is still unable to provide a firm return date. Aaron Wilson of KPRC2 provided a quote from Ryans, stating he is "still seeing how [Collins] progresses with his recovery."

As Collins continues to deal with the hamstring strain, he is currently not expected to play in the team's Week 3 divisional matchup against the Indianapolis Colts .

A two-time Pro Bowler, Collins was the Texans' leading receiver each of the previous three seasons, and led the team with 75 receiving yards in Week 1. The combination of his 6'4" frame and high-end speed gives him an elite catch radius. His ability to haul in contested catches makes him an extremely valuable red zone threat, and one that the Texans were clearly missing on Sunday.

If Houston wants to avoid another sluggish offensive season, getting Collins back to full health will be crucial.

articles.title: Jerry Jeudy, Denzel Boston’s reps signal a chance: Browns offensive snap counts
articles.summary: There’s a new No. 1 receiver in town.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns ' offense struggled in the first half, but not due to quarterback play. They shot themselves in the foot with procedural errors or penalties. Late in the second half, they were only 1-of-9 on third downs, consistently being in long third down situations. But on the final drive, with a bunch of manageable situations, they went 4-of-4 to finish a respectable 5-of-13 on third down. This is stuff to build on, giving a glimpse of maybe, just maybe, Deshaun Watson being serviceable to this offense after all.

Below, we analyze the snap counts and stats on offense for the Cleveland Browns ' Week 2 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

24-of-30 (80%) for 238 yards, 2 TD. 7 carries, 22 yards (3.1 YPC).

In what I'll deem to be his best game as a member of the Browns, QB Deshaun Watson seemed to do everything right. He completed 80% of his passes, didn't turn the ball over, was accurate, and succeeded with pressure in his face. According to Pro Football Focus, he was the team's highest-graded offensive player with an 88.8.

What we said about Watson before still holds true. He is in the unique position where, yes, it makes sense to give leeway to a guy who is coming off of two Achilles' injuries as needing to get back into a rhythm. However, he also gets less leeway because we saw a bad product from him consistently prior to that. If this is the start of a turnaround, it's up to him to continue making that happen.

12 carries, 21 yards (1.8 YPC). 5 catches, 27 yards (5 targets).

2 carries, 4 yards (2.0 YPC). 1 catch, 7 yards (1 target).

The Browns' running game needs to get going. Todd Monken was asked about it on Monday, and said it hasn't been good enough. Nonetheless, Quinshon Judkins still got a solid grade from PFF, in part due to his receptions and decent pass blocking grade.

With Dylan Sampson out, instead of giving Raheim Sanders an increased load, those backup reps were split between he and Jaleel McLaughlin .

6 catches, 28 yards (6 targets). 1 carry, -6 yards (-6.0 YPC).

Here we were talking up KC Concepcion all of training camp and the preseason, and its Denzel Boston who has taken over the team. He led the team in receiving reps and had the breakaway touchdown for Cleveland. You can see how Watson likes throwing to a big target like him, giving him that degree of trust with his radius. Boston was the third-highest graded player on offense by PFF, with a grade of 69.8.

You can see how Jerry Jeudy's role has diminished, as he only played 59% of the snaps, third highest on the team. Jeudy slipped coming out of his break on his one target. To his credit, he helped with a block on the touchdown to Blake Whiteheart .

Tylan Wallace received 25% of the receiving snaps for the second straight week. Isaiah Bond only played four snaps, but caught one pass for a first down.

We got some more involvement from Harold Fannin this week, and he continues to be a load to try to bring down. The Browns were going to have him take a snap on a quarterback tush push, but the Browns false started.

For blocking, Fannin's grades continue to be no good. Blake Whiteheart had a solid day in the blocking department, though, so they balance each other out a little.

This was not the best day for Tytus Howard , who had some penalties and also appeared to yield at least one sack. He was the team's lowest-graded pass blocker this week, and was even worse in the run blocking department.

Spencer Fano had a nice second game, grading out to a 72.9 by PFF (second-highest on offense). He received high marks in both pass and run blocking.

Overall, the guards ( Zion Johnson , 48.4 and Austin Barber , 47.0) received poor grades from PFF too. However, Barber did extremely well in pass blocking, but was lackluster in run blocking. The same goes for Johnson overall.

On Sunday afternoon, the New Orleans Saints picked up their first win of the season on the road against Lamar Jackson and the Baltimore Ravens , in epic comeback fashion. Still, it wasn't all positive vibes for the Saints that afternoon, as offensive lineman Kelvin Banks Jr. went down with an ankle injury that caused him to be carted off the field.

articles.standfirst: Sebastián Villa atacó a Davoo Xeneize y La Cobra: la dura respuesta de los streamers de Boca Juniors
articles.summary: Sebastián Villa atacó a Davoo Xeneize y La Cobra: la dura respuesta de los streamers de Boca Juniors
articles.body: El delantero colombiano de Boca Juniors, Sebastián Villa, arremetió con dureza contra los reconocidos streamers argentinos Davoo Xeneize y La Cobra, luego de las reiteradas críticas que ambos creadores de contenido han expresado hacia su rendimiento y su situación en el club xeneize. En una conversación con el influencer colombiano Chanty, el atacante no se guardó nada y apuntó hacia la exposición que tienen los creadores de contenido en plataformas digitales. "De ellos no hablo, no le doy de comer a esa gente. No me gusta vender humo. Respeto mucho a los streamers, pero hay muchos que hablan de más. La Cobra al lado mío es muy chiquitito, Davo también es así de chiquitito. No les he hecho nada; solo porque son simpatizantes de Boca, creen que tienen el derecho de estar difamando a la persona", aseguró el futbolista. Villa agregó que no conoce personalmente a los streamers y que solo ha visto algunos fragmentos de sus transmisiones en TikTok, remarcando la dificultad de la profesión futbolística: "Creen que ser futbolista es fácil, pero ser futbolista es muy difícil". Las reacciones de los creadores de contenido no tardaron en llegar: "Si yo en mi opinión critico a Villa, ¿por qué él no puede criticarme a mí? Yo lo critico a él, él me critica a mí y está perfecto, cada uno tiene su opinión. Lo que menos necesita Boca es puterío". "No invierto mi tiempo en gente que me insulta a mí o a mis amigos. Obviamente le deseo lo mejor, que haga un montón de goles en Boca. Nunca necesité entrar en polémicas para estar donde estoy". En el ámbito futbolístico, la situación del atacante colombiano en Boca Juniors ha estado bajo la lupa. Ha tenido presencia en 9 partidos de la liga local (solo uno jugando los 90 minutos completos), registrando 0 goles y 1 asistencia. En el apartado internacional, ha sido sumado a las rotaciones del equipo tanto en Copa Sudamericana como en el torneo local mientras busca afianzarse nuevamente como titular en el esquema xeneize.

articles.title: La dura confesión de Hernán Torres por su salida de Millonarios: "Me usaron como carne de cañón"
articles.standfirst: Hernán Torres destapa la verdadera razón de su salida de Millonarios con una contundente frase
articles.summary: Hernán Torres destapa la verdadera razón de su salida de Millonarios con una contundente frase
articles.body: El director técnico ibaguereño Hernán Torres, recordado por haber conquistado en 2012 la decimocuarta estrella que acabó con la sequía de 24 años sin títulos de Millonarios, volvió a referirse a su reciente y breve segundo paso por el banquillo embajador. En una reveladora entrevista otorgada al periodista Diego Rueda en su canal de YouTube, el estratega dejó una frase contundente que encendió el debate en el entorno azul. Torres, quien estuvo al frente del equipo en un segundo ciclo comprendido entre agosto de 2025 y enero de 2026, abordó por primera vez de manera frontal los pormenores de su desvinculación tras solo cinco meses en el cargo. Aunque inició su intervención expresando su profundo respeto hacia la institución capitalina, no se guardó nada sobre las circunstancias que rodearon su salida. "Yo no quiero hablar de Millonarios, porque a Millonarios le debo mucho. No voy a hablar de Millonarios porque es una empresa que yo quiero mucho, me ha dado cosas grandes, me dio el primer título de mi vida, y no soy el que mando en Millonarios", comenzó diciendo el entrenador. Sin embargo, Torres pasó a relatar una anécdota ocurrida a su llegada al club que terminó anticipando su efímero periodo en la dirección técnica: "Pero sí le voy a decir una cosa a usted. Hay un periodista que, cuando yo llegué, fue y me enfrentó. Me dijo: 'a usted lo están usando de carne de cañón, y lo están utilizando. Se lo digo porque a mí me dijeron que a usted lo van a sacar'. Y tenía razón, ya. Ahí le contesto yo", sentenció Torres. El retorno de Hernán Torres a la dirección técnica de Millonarios se dio en agosto de 2025 con el objetivo de apagar incendios tras la salida de David González. No obstante, los resultados deportivos no lo acompañaron y la directiva decidió apartarlo del cargo en enero de 2026. Posteriormente, el equipo pasó por las manos de Fabián Bustos hasta el regreso de Alberto Gamero al banquillo 'embajador' en septiembre de 2026. Las declaraciones de Torres reabrieron el debate sobre la gestión directiva de Millonarios y el trato hacia los entrenadores que asumen el reto en momentos de crisis de resultados.

articles.title: Incendio forestal en Villa de Leyva fuera de control: más de 300 hectáreas afectadas y la emergencia continúa
articles.standfirst: Alerta en Villa de Leyva: voraz incendio forestal consume 300 hectáreas y desata la emergencia
articles.summary: Alerta en Villa de Leyva: voraz incendio forestal consume 300 hectáreas y desata la emergencia
articles.body: Una grave emergencia ambiental mantiene en alerta máxima al municipio de Villa de Leyva. El incendio forestal que se inició el sábado 19 de septiembre en el sector de La Marmolera y el cerro San Marcos, en la vereda La Castellana, continúa activo y ha consumido cerca de 290 a 300 hectáreas de vegetación nativa y cobertura vegetal. Las autoridades locales decretaron la calamidad pública con el fin de agilizar la movilización de recursos y el despliegue de personal técnico y de socorro en los puntos más críticos de la montaña. Más de 300 personas —entre integrantes de los Cuerpos de Bomberos de Boyacá y Cundinamarca, la Defensa Civil, Cruz Roja, Policía Nacional (PONALSAR), el Ejército Nacional y brigadistas voluntarios— trabajan incansablemente para contener la conflagración. Las operaciones en terreno se ven reforzadas desde el aire por cuatro helicópteros equipados con sistemas Bambi Bucket, los cuales realizan descargas de agua continuas para sofocar los focos de calor en zonas de difícil acceso topográfico. El director de la Unidad Nacional para la Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres (UNGRD) en la región y las autoridades locales han señalado que los fuertes vientos, las altas temperaturas y la pendiente del terreno han dificultado severamente las maniobras de sofocación, provocando la reactivación de varios frentes de fuego durante las últimas horas. El gobernador de Boyacá, Carlos Amaya, dio tranquilidad a la comunidad respecto a la protección del casco urbano colonial y sus viviendas, pero enfatizó que la temporada de sequía y el fenómeno de El Niño exigen máxima precaución: "Tenemos el personal y las capacidades para evitar afectaciones en el casco urbano. Sin embargo, el fenómeno de El Niño no es un juego; un incendio forestal se sale de control en cuestión de minutos." Las labores del Puesto de Mando Unificado (PMU) continúan activas para lograr el control total de la conflagración en los próximos días.

articles.title: Series recap: Bees win final series of the season in Albuquerque
articles.summary: Bees see an enchanted ending to end the season on a high note
articles.body:
The Salt Lake Bees (28-46/67-81) ended their season in the Land of Enchantment this past week, looking to finish on a high note in Albuquerque. The squad from Utah did just that, taking four of six from the Isotopes (34-41/73-77) including a 20-hit, 14-run barrage in the 2026 season finale. The Land of Enchantment played host to the Bees' final hurrah of the campaign and created some much needed closure for the Bees in the 148-game season.

Salt Lake brushed off the frustration of the final homestand, winning the first three games of the six-game set. The Bees used four walks and a single in the eighth on Tuesday to comeback from a 4-1 score, eventually winning 7-5 in 10 innings, their 15th extra-inning victory of the year. A pair of longballs, including one from Mr. September, Niko Kavadas , fueled Salt Lake to a 7-2 win. Joel Hurtado was brilliant on the mound in his last Triple-A effort of the year, allowing one run in five innings of work.

The Bees made it three straight wins, taking Thursday's matinee 10-5. Raudi Rodriguez's three-hit, three RBI afternoon paced the side to the comfortable victory, never trailing in the day game. Mother Nature brought the win streak to a screeching halt, stopping Friday's game early in the sixth inning. Salt Lake could not generate much offense before the rain fell, while two unearned runs helped Albuquerque take a 3-0 win.

Weather again impacted action at Isotopes Park, delaying Saturday's showdown by an hour. Albuquerque's Edouard Julien drove in four runs as the Isotopes rolled to an 8-2 win. Logan Porter 's seventh-inning solo homer and Rodriguez' RBI single kept the Bees from being shutout for a second straight night. In the season finale, Salt Lake fell behind 5-0 after two Albuquerque homers off Sam Aldegheri . However, it would be the Bees who stole the show on Sunday, scoring 14 of the game's final 16 runs en route to a 14-7 victory. Five different Bees managed three-or-more hits on Sunday, led by Rodriguez's and Vera's four-hit ledgers.

The Salt Lake bullpen was excellent, allowing one earned run over the six innings of relief. Salt Lake's victory on Sunday secured the ninth series win of the year and gave them 67 total wins, their most in a campaign since the 2024 season. The Bees finished eighth in the final Pacific Coast League standings with a final record of 67-81 over their 148 games played.

Nelson Rada, the Los Angeles Angels ' sixth-ranked prospect on their top-30 list, had himself a nice finish to the year. The outfielder, who will fight for a spot on the Angels' roster come Spring Training, finished the six-game set playing in all six games and batting 10-for-25 (.400) with three doubles, two of which came in the final game, three RBIs and five walks. He stole his 43rd base in the final game, putting him just one shy of Jordyn Adams ' single-season franchise record of 44, set in 2023. The left fielder also had another three-hit game, his fourth in September. With his performance, he extended his hitting streak to five games. Rada finished his full season as a Bee slashing .278/.376/.363 with a .739 OPS.

Raudi Rodriguez, the Halos' 17th-ranked prospect, finished the season with his first career four-hit game at the Triple-A level, with all four hits coming on singles. He also extended his hitting streak to five games, getting things started in Sunday's contest with a base hit. Rodriguez finished the series going 10-for-26 (.385) with six RBIs, five walks, five strikeouts and four runs scored.

The outfielder didn't commit a single error in his 38 games played with Salt Lake. His stellar performance in the outfield looked a lot like his counterpart Nelson Rada, as both young outfielders will be fighting for a higher position within the Halos organization moving forward. Wednesday starter Joel Hurtado, ranked as the Angels' No. 27 prospect, delivered his fifth consecutive outing of five or more innings. Over 91 pitches, the right-hander allowed just one run on two hits while striking out four and walking four.

Hurtado would have preferred a stronger showing in his debut stint with Salt Lake, finishing with a 7.57 ERA, 30 strikeouts and 21 walks across 35.2 innings. Still, the Dominican Republic native showed his ability to go deep into games while relying on an impressive repertoire that continues to support his top-30 prospect status. Cutting down on the walks will be a key focus for Hurtado moving forward.

The Bees closed out another summer of baseball at The Ballpark at America First Square. From record-breaking crowds to firework shows that lit up the Utah sky, to theme nights and giveaways that connected the community, Bees fans had plenty of reasons to make their way to the ballpark throughout the season. With the season now wrapped up, fans should be excited that it's only 186 days until another great season of America's pastime in South Jordan.

With the 2026 campaign officially in the books, Salt Lake looks ahead to Opening Day of the 2027 Pacific Coast League season. The Bees welcome the El Paso Chihuahuas to The Ballpark at America First Square on Friday, March 26, to open the third home schedule in South Jordan.

I don't know about you, but I already miss baseball even though there are still two series to go. For the St. Louis Cardinals , those final 6 games of the 2026 campaign will be completed on the road with the first stop being in Pittsburgh starting Tuesday night. There's little at stake other than pride, but there are some individual player achievements that are possible for St. Louis.

Tuesday night – Andre Pallante (RHP 12-7, 3.70 ERA, 104 SO) vs Jared Jones (RHP 4-6, 4.17 ERA, 109 SO)

Wednesday night – Matthew Liberatore (LHP 5-14, 5.36 ERA, 148 SO) vs TBD

Thursday – Kyle Leahy (RHP 10-5, 3.65 ERA, 129 SO) vs Paul Skenes (RHP 10-11, 3.91 ERA, 192 SO)

Pittsburgh Pirates Jared Jones has won 2 of his last 3 starts, but his most recent outing on September 16 was a no-decision against the Brewers as he threw 5 innings allowing 7 hits and 3 earned runs. Paul Skenes has only won 1 of his last 3 starts and his most recent was not memorable as he allowed 6 hits and 5 earned runs on September 18 as he threw 6 innings and got no decision.

Second baseman Brandon Lowe leads the Pirates with 33 home runs and 93 RBI's.

Centerfielder Oneil Cruz has 20 homers and 67 RBI's with a .280 batting average.

First baseman Ryan O'Hearn has 18 homers, 73 RBI's and a .264 average.

Left fielder Bryan Reynolds has 17 home runs, 71 RBI's and a .262 average.

Right fielder Esmerlyn Valdez has 17 homers, 47 RBI's and a .247 average.

It's not breaking news that the Pittsburgh Pirates and St. Louis Cardinals will not be bothered with playoff baseball in October, but there are individual achievements still within reach. As of this writing, Alec Burleson leads the National League in RBI's with 111, but Sal Stewart is right on his heels with 110. Pete Crow-Armstrong trails both of them with 105. Jordan Walker has been stuck at 28 home runs and hasn't launched a long ball since September 1 against the Dodgers . I would love to see him get a couple more to make the 30 home run plateau, but even more would like to see him return to the swing decisions of early 2026 Jordan Walker and not 2025 Jordan Walker. JJ Wetherholt has 17 home runs, but Pittsburgh is his hometown area and he loves hitting at PNC Park. It's not crazy to think he could reach the 20 home run mark before this season is over next weekend.

As we enter the final 6 games of the season, the St. Louis Cardinals are 3 games behind the Pittsburgh Pirates and have the same record as the Miami Marlins . The Washington Nationals only trail St. Louis by 3 games. The Cardinals need to win 5 of the final 6 games to end the season with a .500 record. That seems unlikely with a weekend trip to Milwaukee waiting for the Cardinals, but dominating the Pittsburgh Pirates in their own park would at least give them a fighting chance. We'll see how that goes starting Tuesday night.

articles.title: Taylor Fritz is in danger of coming under real criticism after his latest decision and America’s defeat
articles.summary: Taylor Fritz will return to a tennis court very shortly as he prepares to represent Team World at the 2026 Laver Cup. Fritz last played...
articles.body:
Taylor Fritz will return to a tennis court very shortly as he prepares to represent Team World at the 2026 Laver Cup.

Fritz last played at the US Open , where he suffered a disappointing third round exit against Francisco Cerundolo. He was the ninth seed at the Grand Slam in New York, where Fritz was expected to enjoy a lengthy stay.

It wasn't meant to be, but the home fans were delighted to see his fellow American ATP star Ben Shelton reach the final. However, Shelton lost to Alexander Zverev in his maiden Grand Slam final, ensuring the American men's major title drought will continue into at least 2027. Andy Roddick remains the last American men's Grand Slam champion, having lifted the US Open trophy all the way back in 2003.

There has since been further disappointment for the nation since New York this year, with the USA failing to qualify for the Davis Cup Finals , shocking followers of the team and indeed of the event. Shelton lost his first match since the US Open final , with his nation ultimately falling 3-2 to Czechia.

Notably, there was no appearance from Fritz, who decided to withdraw from the side, alongside Tommy Paul. But Fritz will soon head to London to play in the Laver Cup , which is a scheduling decision that certainly leaves the world number 10 open to criticism, especially after the USA's painful Davis Cup defeat.

Taylor Fritz in danger of criticism after USA's Davis Cup exit

The USA could certainly have done with Fritz against Czechia, who were both playing on home soil and boasted ATP stars such as Jiri Lehecka and Jakub Mensik. The visitors also had a strong side containing Shelton and Learner Tien, but the record 32-time Davis Cup champions fell short.

And Shelton's appearance undoubtedly makes Fritz's absence look much worse, with the former heading straight to Prague after reaching the US Open final, demonstrating fantastic commitment and indeed energy to represent his nation. Moving in the complete opposite direction of Fritz, Shelton has since decided to withdraw from the Laver Cup, having prioritised the Davis Cup qualifiers. He was joined under captain Bob Bryan by Tien, Martin Damm, Christian Harrison and Austin Krajicek.

Of course, nothing should be taken away from Czechia, who played heroic tennis in front of their own fans to secure a famous win. But it definitely could have been a different story if the big-hitting Fritz had decided to make the journey to Prague to play for the USA. He was under no obligation to do so, but it would have gone down very well with American tennis fans.

Home hero Mensik has since shared his delight at reaching the Davis Cup Finals, posting on his Instagram : "There are moments in sport that stay with you forever. This was one of them. Playing for your country is something you can't really put into words. The pressure feels different, the emotions hit harder, and every single point means a little bit more.

"To stand on that court with this team, hear the crowd behind us and fight for every ball together was something truly special. We left everything out there and created a weekend I'll never forget. Thank you to everyone who filled the arena, supported us from the first point until the last and made us feel your energy. This one was for all of us! Bologna [soon]."

Mensik battled past Shelton after two hours and 11 minutes, with his compatriot Lehecka completing the win by defeating Tien. Earlier in the tie, Tien beat Mensik and Lehecka beat Shelton, while Harrison and Krajicek won their doubles tie with Adam Pavlasek and Patrik Rikl.

The Carson Wentz experience — great band name, for the record — is going to be put on the shelf. He'll slide down into being the QB2 yet again due to the Vikings getting the coveted injury update.

QB1 Kyler Murray has cleared the concussion protocol, something that Kevin O'Connell confirmed to the media earlier in the day. Consider the team's official social media description : "Head Coach Kevin O'Connell has announced QB Kyler Murray has cleared the concussion protocol and will start Sunday at Tampa Bay."

Since he's already cleared, Mr. Murray can fully get worked into the mix to prepare for the Week 3 game. The former Cardinal is still relatively new in the Twin Cities. Being able to soak up all of the available reps and coaching help without there being any health hindrances is a good thing and to be coveted.

So far, Murray's Minnesota experience has been so scarce that it's been close to non-existent.

The Week 1 game saw him start before leaving just eleven plays into the contest. At the time, things looked really scary; thankfully, he has been able to come back from his concussion in a reasonably short amount of time. Minnesota was wise to slow play things, letting the veteran to have some extra runway prior to getting back onto the field.

The 29-year-old passer is now looking to get his Vikings stint going yet again. He'll do so from within the context of there being a few hungry mouths to feed at receiver in Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, both of whom have received humble yardage totals due to Minnesota's passer turmoil and the tempest in The Windy City.

Murray went 3/5 for 18 yards in the Week 1 Packers game. He tossed an interception on an ill-advised throw under duress; launching the ball into the heavens while off balance is a terrible decision that usually ends poorly. Was he nervous for that debut Vikings game?

Kyler Murray 's task is to ensure that he makes great decisions in his upcoming opportunities. Both individually and within the players around him, the talent is so ample that only terrible decision making will keep the aerial attack from getting off the ground.

In Week 3, Minnesota goes down to Tampa Bay for a game against what will be a desperate group of pirates since the Buccaneers are down at 0-2. Seeing Murray both start and finish the game is what everyone is looking to see.

articles.title: Bengals snap count takeaways from win over Texans
articles.summary: Some notes about the snap counts from the Bengals' win over the Texans.
articles.body:
Another week, another win for the Cincinnati Bengals that stresses the impressive roster overhaul on the defensive side of the ball and the outright solid depth for all units.

This time, it was a road win over the Houston Texans , a game dominated by Dexter Lawrence and the Bengals defense.

Exiting the victory, Bengals snap counts show expected stuff from Joe Burrow 's offense and some eyebrow-raising depth on Lawrence's defense, especially in the trenches.

Andrei Iosivas , as expected, continues to hold down the third wideout spot at 53 percent of the snaps. Dohnte Meyers got 11 reps and had a bigger role on special teams, while rookie Colbie Young got 10 snaps.

Drew Sample had 36 snaps and Erick All had 25 at tight end as the Bengals shifted formation strategy in the second half to emphasize under-center stuff.

Samaje Perine ate 24 snaps (40 percent), getting some notable usage over Chase Brown (42) snaps at time in an expected, situational rotation.

The edge rotation is deep . Boye Mafe played 57 snaps, while Myles Murphy got 45 and rookie Cashius Howell had 41. Cedric Johnson was super effective on his 23 reps.

Al Golden's defense is somehow even deeper on the inside. Jonathan Allen and Dexter Lawrence each had 50-plus snaps, with Kris Kenkins and TJ Slaton sitting on 29 and 27, respectively.

articles.title: NAU at Montana State: Who Has More to Worry About After Lackluster Week 3?
articles.summary: The ‘Cats and the Lumberjacks didn’t look like themselves last week.
articles.body:
One of the biggest games in the FCS this weekend takes place in Bozeman on Saturday night with #1 Montana State (4-0) hosting #18 Northern Arizona (3-1). As the heart of Big Sky play gets underway, though, both the Bobcats and Lumberjacks enter this primetime contest in a bit of a odd place. Despite both teams getting wins over opponents they should have ran away from last weekend, both fell rather flat and had to scrape it together. Is that cause for concern for one, both or niether of these programs as they begin what they both hope is a run to a conference title and beyond?

The real shocker of the week was MSU's struggle against winless Central Connecticut State. The defending champions have worn the #1 next to their name all season but they looked far from the top team in their 35-30 victory over the Blue Devils. Uncharacteristic mistakes on both sides of the ball made it so Montana State had to battle back from a 21-7 third quarter deficit at home (a place they have only lost two regular season games in the last six seasons) to escape with a win.

Justin Lamson and company got it done but it was not pretty. When the dust had settled the 'Cats had more turnovers, fewer first downs and less time of possession. Had it not been for 14 CCSU penalties that bailed them out, they very well could have ended up on the wrong side of one of the biggest upsets in FCS history as 42.5-point favorites. Is that a harbinger of things to come, though, or… maybe… is it just the wake up call that a team who has now won 18 straight games needed as it comes into the most important part of its season?

"There's not a single excuse we're going to make," said head coach Brent Vigen plainly after the game. "We've got to show up and play. We didn't do that well enough today… every once in a while you find yourselves in these situations and you hope like crazy you get out of them and you can win and you can learn in winning. And we'll do that."

The Bobcats' opponent come in with a similar feeling, albeit one of much lesser magnitude. Northern Arizona had to stave off a pesky Utah Tech squad on the road. The Trailblazers have not even come close to winning a game this year and yet had Brain Wright's team on the ropes in the fourth quarter. The Lumberjacks opened up a two-score lead but only had a four-point edge well into the final 15 minutes. Their 35-23 win was by far the closest defeat that winless Utah Tech has suffered up to this point.

NAU missed on seven of its ten third down attempts and gave the ball away twice, one of which directly led to points for the Trailblazers on a pick six. For a team that many have picked to be at least an at-large qualifier to the postseason this year, there sure appeared to be a lot of dents in the armor last weekend. It's the type of ho-hum win that can go one of two ways; either the Lumberjacks will play incredibly inspired in a much more difficult matchup on Saturday or they'll crumble.

"None of us thought we were playing very well or coaching very well," said Wright following the contest. "But to watch our team stay composed and get ready for the next play is something we can carry with us moving forward."

One thing that should give NAU fans some relief is that, despite the struggles, quarterback Ty Pennington still looked sharp. He completed 18 passes and averaged 11.5 yards per throw with two touchdowns. The connection with receiver Myseth Currie was clicking as he went for five catches and 117 yards. The issue, as it was for Montana State in their game, was largely on defense. The tackles were not all that easy to come by for either team and the failure to wrap up opposing ball carriers hurt.

Both teams have their backs against the wall as they meet up but the eyes on Montana State are a lot more scrutinous. The good news for MSU is that it has faced adversity before. Last year they notably struggled in a similar sort of game against Mercyhurst in the same juncture of the season then went on to win the next week 57-3 over Eastern Washington. Vigen's teams are known for their discipline and ability to weather storms and the same issues rarely rear their heads twice in a row with him in charge. That is something that ought to give 'Cats fans some peace of mind.

What might not, though, is how formidable of an opponent this Northern Arizona team tends to be against them. Last year the Lumberjacks had them in a 7-7 gridlock midway through the second quarter in Flagstaff before MSU eventually pulled away. In 2022 it took a last second field goal for Vigen's team to come out with a 41-38 victory. That game still marks the most points the Bobcats have allowed to a Big Sky team since the turn of the decade.

Someone is going to get a much-needed palate cleanser on Saturday night.

The game will be aired on ESPN2 and will kick off at 10:30 PM (ET).

articles.title: Fans immediately hated the new name for the Detroit Tigers' stadium
articles.summary: Stadium names don't get much worse.
articles.body:
It's the norm in American sports for stadiums to change names as new corporate sponsors get in on naming-rights deals. But for some stadiums, they have the same name for so long that it becomes part of the local vernacular.

In Detroit , Comerica Park was certainly one of those stadiums. And to make matters worse, its new name will be among the worst stadium names across all of the major sports.

The Tigers announced on Monday that Comerica Park — which had been the stadium's name for its entire 26-year history — will be renamed to Fifth Third Park starting in the 2027 season (if that happens). A merger between Comerica and Fifth Third finalized earlier this year, and Fifth Third plans to phase out the Comerica brand in the coming months.

The result: A fraction is now sponsoring a baseball stadium.

I have a hard time believing that people in Detroit will actually call it anything other than Comerica Park. It's the same way Acrisure Stadium still goes by "Heinz Field" to everyone in Pittsburgh .

But we can understand why fans were upset with the name change. It's just bad.

articles.title: Kentucky's Castell cashes in on the road vs Texas A&M
articles.summary: Kentucky safety Jordan Castell earned national honors after his standout performance in the Wildcats' 31-21 upset win.
articles.body:
A week after the Kentucky Wildcats watched a 17-13 halftime cushion against Alabama dissolve into a 45-17 defeat, safety Jordan Castell delivered the signature performance of the Wildcats' season—and it's now been rewarded on a national stage. Castell has been named the Panini Senior Bowl Defensive Player of the Week after anchoring Kentucky's 31-21 upset of No. 9 Texas A&M on the road, a result that ended the Aggies' stay in the Associated Press top 10, dropping 14 spots to No. 23 in the Sundays AP Top 25 latest drop.

The senior transfer's line speaks for itself: a game-high 13 tackles, a pass breakup and, with 6:34 to play, an interception in Kentucky's own territory that snuffed out Texas A&M 's best chance at a comeback. Marcel Reed never saw him coming. The Aggies' quarterback finished 26 of 49 for 236 yards with a touchdown and two picks—a rough follow-up to a start that had him among the SEC's hottest passers through two weeks.

It wasn't Castell's first big moment at Kyle Field. He intercepted a pass in the same building a year earlier while at Florida , giving him takeaways there in back-to-back seasons for two different SEC programs. That's no coincidence. Castell left Florida for Kentucky this offseason largely to reunite with defensive coordinator Jay Bateman, who coached him early in his college career—and who came to Lexington straight off two seasons running Texas A&M's own defense.

Bateman wasn't the only one in Kentucky's defensive backfield room with Aggieland ties. Assistant safeties coach Trey Odom spent time in 2024 as a graduate assistant working with Texas A&M's defensive backs, part of a staff that signed three top-25 cornerbacks that recruiting cycle. Between Bateman calling the plays and Odom helping prep the safeties, Kentucky's game plan for stopping the Aggies had inside knowledge built into it from top to bottom—and it showed.

The unit delivered. Kentucky intercepted Reed twice — linebacker Sam Greene had the other, the first pick of his career — and stuffed Texas A&M on three separate fourth-down tries, repeatedly flipping field position against a team that opened as a 16.5-point favorite. First-year head coach Will Stein pointed to that identity afterward, saying his defense played with "the physicality... the toughness... the grit" he wants every week.

Kentucky's offense held up its end too. The Wildcats broke a 7-7 tie with 21 unanswered points in the third quarter, powered by quarterback Kenny Minchey 's 252-yard, two-touchdown day and running back CJ Baxter, who scored twice and crossed 1,000 career rushing yards along the way. But the day belonged to the defense—Kentucky's first win at Kyle Field since 1952—and to Castell most of all.

The Wildcats (2-1, 1-1 SEC) stay home to host South Alabama this weekend. Texas A&M heads to Baton Rouge to face LSU , the first stop on a stretch that looks a lot less forgiving after Saturday.
authors: Lee Ann Herring Olvedo, UK Wildcats Wire

articles.title: Why Puka Nacua isn't playing for Rams vs. Giants with injury news
articles.summary: The Rams are already behind the eight ball to start the 2026 NFL season, and now must take on the improved Giants without their most potent offensive weapon.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams are already behind the eight ball to start the 2026 NFL season, after a heavy defeat to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia.

They are looking to right the ship in Week 2 but have a difficult task as they welcome an improved New York Giants team to SoFi Stadium for a primetime Monday Night Football matchup.

The task was already difficult given their opponent's impressive Week 1 victory over the Dallas Cowboys , in which they look strong in John Harbaugh's debut at the helm, but it's now even more daunting given their star wide receiver will miss tonight's game.

The Sporting News brings you the latest on Puka Nacua 's status for the primetime matchup, and why he has not taken the field.

Puka Nacua has been listed as inactive by the Rams for their Week 2 match against the New York Giants at SoFi Stadium on Monday night.

The star wide receiver tested his injury on the field before the game, but decided he wasn't healthy enough to participate.

The move wasn't unexpected, since there were reports that his status for the game was trending down , but still made headlines as it had not yet been confirmed until inactives were released ahead of kickoff.

Rams star wide receiver Puka Nacua officially has a hip/groin injury.

After Thursday's practice, Rams head coach Sean McVey said that Nacua "didn't feel totally like himself." He then appeared on the injury report for the first time Friday, sitting out the team's second practice of the week.

He also did not participate in Saturday's practice and was officially listed as questionable for the game.

The issue is especially concerning given the Rams had additional time off between their Week 1 and Week 2 games, having flown back from their season opener in Australia.

articles.title: A Manning is set to play at Neyland once again, but Arch has never even been to Knoxville
articles.summary: Saturday will be his first trip.
articles.body:
For the first time in nearly three decades, a Manning — wearing No. 16 — will play at Neyland Stadium. He just won't be wearing the right shade of orange.

Arch Manning will lead his No. 1 ranked Texas Longhorns into Knoxville on Saturday, a place that he's never been. Manning, one of the highest profile prospects of all time, never visited Tennessee during his recruiting process. Being born in 2004 with uncle Peyton already in the NFL, there's really never been a reason. That changes this weekend.

"Yeah, it's interesting, Arch and I, we were meeting this morning. And I just had assumed he'd been to Knoxville and been to Tennessee," Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said on Monday. "He's never been before. So I'm sure it's pretty, for the family, for Arch, to play on the field that his uncle played on. And that's, again, just another, it's all part of the journey. It's all part of the story. And so for him, I'm sure there's gonna be a special moment in there for the family and for him."

Manning ended up choosing Texas over both Alabama and Georgia after taking official visits to all three schools. While it may be a bit strange for Peyton this weekend in Knoxville, it's likely just another start in the SEC on the road for Arch.

"I think at the end of the day, you're the quarterback at Texas," Sarkisian said. "Your last name's Manning. Regardless of what you do, you're gonna get critiqued. You're going to get criticized. I'm the head coach of Texas. Regardless of what I do, I'm going to get critiqued. I'm gonna get criticized. Who really gives a crap? Just go play, man. Go be you."

Manning is in his second season as the starter at Texas. It's been an up and down ride to this point, filled with inconsistencies and elite flashes. His struggles in true road games have been noted (2-2 record in 2025), capped with an ugly loss in Athens, 35-10.

His next environment could be his toughest test yet.

"We're going into what I would probably consider is the loudest stadium in the country, Neyland Stadium," Sarkisian said.

"It's 100 and something thousand, I don't know the exact number of what it holds — 102,000 103,000, similar to our place. But the structure of it is what it is, their fans are engaged, they understand football, they got a lot of pride in their program. But I don't know, the structure of it, why, if it's more vertical, I'm not sure why."

Arch's first trip to Neyland begins at noon ET, with College Gameday on site and the whole college football world watching. Texas enters as a 5.5 point favorite.
